'''Shreeram Shankar Abhyankar''' (22 July 1930 – 2 November 2012)<ref>{{cite web|title=S. S. Abhyankar (1930–2012)|url=https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/104/01/0131.pdf|publisher=Current Science.ac.in|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130316094457/http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/104/01/0131.pdf|archive-date=2013-03-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=by SR Ghorpade|title=Remembering Shreeram S. Abhyankar|url=https://www.asiapacific-mathnews.com/03/0301/0022_0030.pdf|publisher=Asia Pacific Mathematics Newsletter|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618060920/http://www.asiapacific-mathnews.com/03/0301/0022_0030.pdf|archive-date=2013-06-18}}</ref>  was an [[Indian American]] [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to [[algebraic geometry]]. At the time of his death, he held the Marshall [[Distinguished Professor]] of Mathematics Chairman at [[Purdue University]], and was also a professor of computer science and industrial engineering. He is known for [[Abhyankar's conjecture]] of finite [[group theory]]. His later research was in the area of [[computation]]al and [[algorithm]]ic [[algebraic geometry]].

==Career==
Abhyankar was born during the late [[British Raj]], 22 July 1930, in a [[Marathi people|Marathi]] [[Chitpavan]] [[Brahmin]] family in [[Ujjain]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]]. He earned his B.Sc. from the [[Royal Institute of Science]] of [[University of Mumbai]] in 1951, his [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] at [[Harvard University]] in 1952, and his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1955. His thesis, written under the direction of [[Oscar Zariski]], was titled ''Local uniformization on algebraic surfaces over modular ground fields''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=16462}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Abhyankar.html|title=Abhyankar biography|publisher=|access-date=20 January 2017}}</ref> Before going to [[Purdue]], he was an associate [[professor of mathematics]] at [[Cornell University]] and [[Johns Hopkins University]].

Abhyankar was appointed the Marshall Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at Purdue in 1967. His research topics include [[algebraic geometry]] (particularly [[resolution of singularities]], a field in which he made significant progress over fields of finite characteristic), [[commutative algebra]], [[local algebra]], [[valuation theory]], theory of functions of [[several complex variables]], [[quantum electrodynamics]], [[circuit theory]], [[invariant theory]], [[combinatorics]], [[computer-aided design]], and [[robotics]]. He popularized the [[Jacobian conjecture]].

==Death==
Abhyankar died of a heart condition on 2 November 2012 at his residence near Purdue University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Shreeram S. Abhyankar. Obituary.|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/JCOnline/obituary.aspx?n=Shreeram-S-Abhyankar&pid=160872790|access-date=24 November 2012}}</ref>

==Honours==
Abhyankar has won numerous awards and honours.
* Abhyankar received the Herbert Newby McCoy Award from Purdue University in 1973 .
* Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]
* Editorial board member of the ''Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics''
* [[Chauvenet Prize]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (1978)<ref>{{cite journal|author=Abhyankar, Shreeram|title=Historical ramblings in algebraic geometry and related algebra|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=83|year=1976|issue=6|pages=409–448|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/historical-ramblings-in-algebraic-geometry-and-related-algebra|doi=10.2307/2318338|jstor=2318338}}</ref>
* Honorary Doctorate Degree (Docteur Honoris Causa) by the [[University of Angers]] in France (29 October 1998)
*Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012)<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-03.</ref>

==Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana==
{{Infobox institute
| image = Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana.jpg
| established = 1976
| founder = Shreeram Abhyankar
| location = [[Erandwane]]
| city = [[Pune]]
| state = [[Maharashtra]]
| country = [[India]]
| website = {{URL|https://www.bprim.org/}}
}}
'''Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana''' is a research and education institute for [[mathematics]] in [[Pune]], [[India]], founded by Abhyankar. The institute is named after the great ancient Indian Mathematician [[Bhāskara II|Bhaskaracharya]] (Born in 1114 A.D). It was founded in 1976.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bprim.org/more.htm |title=Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana Home Page |access-date=2009-10-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213041443/http://www.bprim.org/more.htm |archive-date=2009-12-13 }}</ref> It has researchers working in many areas of mathematics, particularly in [[algebra]] and [[number theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bprim.org/people.php#A |title=Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana Home Page - people at BP |access-date=16 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213005516/http://www.bprim.org/people.php#A |archive-date=13 December 2009 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Since 1992, the Pratishthan has also been a recognized center for conducting [[Regional Mathematics Olympiad]] (RMO) under the [[National Board for Higher Mathematics]] (NBHM) for Maharashtra and Goa Region.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana Official Website|url=https://www.bprim.org/}}</ref>

Pratishthana publishes the mathematics periodical ''Bona Mathematica'' and has published texts in higher and Olympiad mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bprim.org/publication.php |title=Bhasakracharya Pratishthana Home Page |access-date=2009-10-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091010194326/http://www.bprim.org/publication.php |archive-date=2009-10-10 }}</ref> Besides this the Pratishthan holds annual / biennial conferences/ Workshops in some research areas in higher mathematics attended by Indian/Foreign scholars and Professors. The Pratishthan has organized a number of workshops for research students and college teachers under the aegis of NBHM/NCM. The National Board for Higher Mathematics has greatly helped Pratishthan to enrich its library. The [[Department of Atomic Energy]] and the Mathematics Department of S. P. [[Savitribai Phule Pune University|Pune University]] have rendered active co-operation in holding conferences/workshops.

It also conducts the BMTSC exam which is a school-level mathematics competition for students studying in the 5th and the 6th grade. The objectives of the competition are listed below:
1. Identify good students of mathematics at an early age.
2. A pre Olympiad type competition.
3. To enhance Mathematical ability and logical thinking.
4. Nurture programs for successful students to improve their ability.
